explanation: A bitmap is a data structure that uses an array of bits to represent the status of resources, such as whether a block or object is free (0) or in use (1). It is used in file systems and other applications to efficiently track and manage available resources, minimizing storage overhead by dedicating just one bit per resource.
syntax: void set_bit(unsigned char *bitmap, int index, int value);
code_example: unsigned char bitmap[1] = {0};  // Initialize a single-byte bitmap
bitmap[0] |= (1 << 0);  // Set bit 0 to 1 (indicating in use)
if (bitmap[0] & (1 << 0)) {  // Check if bit 0 is set
example_explanation: This example demonstrates a simple bitmap by initializing a byte array, setting the first bit to 1 to indicate a resource is in use, and then checking that bit to confirm its status. It shows how bitwise operations can efficiently manage resource allocation in a bitmap.
